She tries to make phonetic connections with Turkish and English words so that students can remember characters or words easily. Also she is very patient and repeats everything if a point is not clear. I think what  is missing in this class is some board-writing. As the language is alien to the students in most cases, pinyin of the words or the characters can get easily mixed up. The textbook's explanations are not enough and easy to get lost. Therefore writing the basics of each subject on the board would make the class easy to follow and more active.

This course, as the language immensely differs from the languages most students know, can be hard to get used to. Chinese 1 could be more complicated and a bit unexpected compared to other language courses, for students who does not really try to spend time to learn Chinese outside class. Hardest parts is the tones and thus, listening. 
However because it is different from all other languages, it also can be fun and interesting. The grammar is the easiest I've seen, too.
